agentCan: Run the entire CLI workflow: create, configure, upload, submit, and poll app status
Implement the PKCE flow (fresh state and code_verifier per authorization) and refresh handling
Host the install link and build fresh authorize URLs per user

approval.cost: No fee, price, or paid tier for app review is stated anywhere in the documentation read
approval.trigger: For public apps: 'A public app needs Brevo's review before other accounts can authorize it', and 'a public app can be authorized by any Brevo account once Brevo has reviewed and approved it'. Pre-approval, NO account outside your organisation can authorize the app at all (an absolute cap, not numeric; no numeric user/install cap is stated for approved apps). Process: brevo app upload (at least once, all required fields filled; brevo app submit lists missing fields), brevo app submit, confirm the submission statement, then complete and send the browser submission form ('Your app is submitted only when you complete and send that form'). Track via brevo app status (draft / submitted / in_review / approved / rejected / changes_requested); reviewer feedback arrives by email only. Brevo does NOT list public apps on any marketplace: distribution is your own install link or third-party marketplaces.
approval.wait: 'Brevo emails you the decision, generally within 7 days' (stated)

blockers.detail: 'brevo app upload refuses a changed distribution_type. To move an integration from private to public, create a new public app.' Non-interactive creation defaults to private, so scripted setup that forgets --distribution public silently creates the wrong app.
blockers.howToClear: Pass --distribution public explicitly at creation; verify distribution before building on the app.
blockers.title: One-way door: distribution type is fixed at creation

blockers.detail: Public apps have no client secret by design. Any architecture assuming a confidential client breaks; PKCE (S256) is mandatory, your server builds a fresh authorize URL (new state and code_verifier) for every authorization, and the refresh request also omits client_secret.
blockers.howToClear: Design as a PKCE public client from the start.
blockers.title: Public apps have no client secret

blockers.detail: Edit auth.scopes, upload, then submit again and wait for the email decision. Withdrawing an approved app likewise removes it from availability, and restoring it means re-submitting and going 'through the review again'.
blockers.howToClear: Batch scope needs before the first submission; treat the approved scope set as a release.
blockers.title: Scope changes on an approved app require a new review

tested: Read-only verification: the CLI app lifecycle, distribution model, review process and timeline, PKCE shape, and scope rules were checked against current developers.brevo.com pages (no app created, nothing submitted)
unverified: Any cost/fee for creating or reviewing a public app (none mentioned).
Any numeric cap on users, installs, or authorizations for an approved public app (none stated; gating is account-based).
The full enumerated list of required submission fields (docs give logo_uri as an example and say brevo app submit lists missing fields at runtime; no complete published checklist).
Substantive review criteria beyond agreement to the Brevo Developer Terms and submission completeness.
Any cap on number of apps per account or redirect URIs per app (the --redirect-uri flag is documented as repeatable).

alternatives: OAuth app, private distribution (confidential client with client_secret; only users within your own Brevo organisation can authorize it; 'it works as soon as you create it', no review)

Machine-to-machine (M2M) app (client-credentials style, no user or consent screen; Brevo's 'recommended default for new server-to-server work', but always private: it authenticates as your own account and cannot connect customers)
Plain API key ('Copy key from dashboard', lifetime 'Until revoked'; your own account only, not a per-user consent mechanism)
flavor.recommended: An OAuth app with public distribution, authorization code flow with PKCE (S256) and no client secret
flavor.why: The object is a Brevo app (an 'OAuth app') created and managed with the Brevo CLI (@getbrevo/cli), not a web portal. Every app has a distribution type set once at creation: private or public. 'A public app can be authorized by any Brevo account once Brevo has reviewed and approved it.' Scopes follow the pattern {resource}:{action} (e.g. contacts:read, transactional.email:write); new apps are seeded with contacts:read, contacts:write, crm:read, crm:write.

humanMust: Sign in via brevo login (your own Brevo account; credentials saved to ~/.brevo/credentials.json)
Agree to the Brevo Developer Terms at public app creation (the --accept-developer-terms flag / y/N prompt) and confirm the submission statement
Complete and send the browser submission form after brevo app submit (the app 'is submitted only when you complete and send that form')
Read the review decision in email (brevo app status shows state, never the feedback)
name: Brevo
nuances: Scopes don't imply each other: ':write does not imply :read. Request both if your app needs both.' Requested scopes must be a subset of the scopes registered on the app, otherwise invalid_scope; the token response's granted scope 'may be narrower than what you requested', so use it to detect missing permissions.
Scope typos surface late: brevo app upload validates scope format locally but does 'not cross-check against the IdP catalog. Typos surface as invalid_scope errors at authorization time'.

Refresh-token rotation: 'Always store the new access_token, and if a new refresh_token is returned, replace the stored one.' Refresh tokens are valid for 30 days; access tokens 1 hour; authorization codes expire in 10 minutes ('exchange it immediately').
CLI credential trap: brevo logout 'clears cached app credentials (client ID / client secret)'; run brevo app credentials --reveal-secret before logging out if you need them saved.

App-type ceilings: M2M apps are private-only, and 'UI apps can't be public for now': public distribution is consent-based OAuth apps only. The local app-config.json must be in sync with Brevo's copy or submit stops and shows the diff.
prerequisites: Node.js >= 20.15.0 and the Brevo CLI (@getbrevo/cli); public apps require CLI 2.5.0 or later
A Brevo account to sign in with
At least one OAuth callback URL; all required listing fields filled (e.g. logo_uri) before submit

steps.detail: npm install -g @getbrevo/cli (also yarn/Homebrew). Requirements: Node.js >= 20.15.0; public apps require CLI 2.5.0 or later.
steps.title: Install the Brevo CLI

steps.detail: brevo login opens oauth-cli.brevo.com in a browser; after signing in to your own Brevo account, credentials are saved to ~/.brevo/credentials.json.
steps.title: Authenticate the CLI

steps.detail: brevo app create --distribution public --redirect-uri <url> --accept-developer-terms (or interactive brevo app create / brevo app init, choosing Public, then OAuth app, then at least one callback URL). Choosing public opens the Brevo Developer Terms; answering no to the agreement cancels creation. Non-interactive runs default to private, so --distribution public must be passed explicitly.
steps.title: Create the app as public

steps.detail: Edit auth.scopes and fields such as logo_uri in app-config.json, then brevo app upload to push the config to Brevo.
steps.title: Configure scopes and listing fields; upload

steps.detail: Your server builds the authorize URL per user (fresh state and PKCE code_verifier each time) pointing at oauth.brevo.com/realms/partner/oauth/authorize, receives the code on the callback (expires in 10 minutes), exchanges it at the token endpoint sending code_verifier instead of a client secret, stores tokens server-side, calls the API with Authorization: Bearer, and refreshes with grant_type=refresh_token (no client_secret).
steps.title: Implement the PKCE flow

steps.detail: The app must have been uploaded at least once with all required fields filled, and local app-config.json must be in sync with Brevo's copy. Run brevo app submit, confirm the submission statement, then complete and send the browser form that opens. Track with brevo app status; the decision arrives by email, 'generally within 7 days'.
steps.time: Submit ~10 min; decision generally within 7 days (stated)
steps.title: Submit for review

steps.detail: Brevo doesn't list public apps anywhere; host your own install link (e.g. a 'Connect Brevo' button). Because of PKCE, your server builds a fresh authorize URL for every authorization.
steps.title: Distribute via your own install link

tagline: A genuine OAuth program managed entirely from a CLI: apps are private or public by a choice fixed at creation, public apps use PKCE with no client secret, and Brevo's review (decision generally within 7 days, by email) stands before any external account can authorize.

time.active: ~30 min of CLI setup + ~half a day of flow code
time.total: About a week: review decision 'generally within 7 days' (stated) plus build time
